title: Optimized CTAB DNA extraction for different tissues
author: Damaris Godinez-Vidal
materials: When working with non-freeze-dried tissue, grind 100 mg of tissue with LN2 to obtain a powder. When working with freeze-dried tissue use warm, fresh CTAB buffer to grind the tissue (Note 3). Add 300 µL of warm, fresh CTAB buffer and incubate samples with light shaking for 60 min at 60-65 ºC (Figure 1A). If the water bath or Thermoblock does not allow for shaking, then shake the samples by hand every 15 min.
Quantify and analyze the genomic DNA (Note 7).

steps.title: Prepare Workspace
steps.instruction: Clean the bench or work space with 70% ethanol and place paper towels near the work area.

steps.title: Pretreat Tissues (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform tissue-specific pretreatment if required before proceeding to buffer addition.

substeps.instruction: For mammalian hair follicles and sperm: Add proteinase K (100 µg/µL) to cover the tissue and incubate for 60 min at 60 ºC.
For cyst nematode eggs and juveniles: Pretreat with proteinase K at 60 ºC for 30 min.
For juvenile nematodes (alternative): Boil for 30 s.

steps.title: Prepare and Warm CTAB Buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh CTAB buffer with the concentration appropriate for the tissue type and warm it to 60-65 ºC.

substeps.instruction: Use 2% CTAB for freeze-dried tissue (e.g., freeze-dried fungal mycelia).
Use 3% CTAB for plant vegetative and reproductive tissue (e.g., leaves and roots), plant seeds, fresh fungal mycelia, nematodes, and arthropods.
Use 4% CTAB for mammalian hair follicles and sperm.

steps.title: Add Tissue and Buffer
steps.instruction: Add powdered tissue to the Eppendorf tube and add CTAB buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add enough powder to fill 100 µL of the tube's volume (can be increased to 250 µL).
Add CTAB buffer; if tissue volume was increased to 250 µL, adjust buffer volume to 500 µL.

steps.title: Perform First Chloroform-Isoamyl Alcohol Wash
steps.instruction: Separate the DNA from proteins and lipids using isoamyl alcohol:chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of isoamyl alcohol:chloroform (24:1) to the tubes.
Vortex the suspension until it turns white.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature.
Recover the upper phase (supernatant) without touching the white interphase and transfer to a new Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Purify Supernatant
steps.instruction: Repeat the isoamyl alcohol:chloroform wash to clear the interface.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of isoamyl alcohol:chloroform (24:1).
Vortex the suspension well.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature.
Recover the upper phase (supernatant) without touching the white interphase and transfer to a new Eppendorf tube.

Repeat this process until the interface is completely transparent or clear (typically 3 washes for nematodes, arthropods, young plant leaves, and freeze-dried tissue; 4 washes for plant seeds, roots, and fungal mycelia; 5 washes for mammalian hair follicles and sperm).

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA using absolute isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of absolute isopropanol.

Incubate from 30 to 40 min at -20 ºC (Note: if tissue was < 30 mg, incubating for 3 hr or more may improve concentration; if tissue was ≥ 100 mg, avoid incubating more than 60 min to prevent contamination).

steps.title: Wash DNA Pellet
steps.instruction: Clean the DNA pellet using ethanol washes.

substeps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 7 min at room temperature.
Wash the pellet with 500 µL of absolute ethanol and vortex until the pellet comes off the bottom of the tube.
Centrifuge at 14,000 rpm for 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Dry the Pellet
steps.instruction: Remove ethanol and dry the pellet.

substeps.instruction: Decant the ethanol using a plastic beaker.
Leave the tubes inverted on a paper towel to dry the pellet for no more than 5 min.

steps.title: Dissolve and Recover DNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in nuclease-free water.

substeps.instruction: Add nuclease-free water to dissolve the pellet (add no more than 40 µL to concentrate DNA; if pellet is not visible, add 20 µL).
Incubate the tubes at 65 ºC for 10 min.
